newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand yields close lower across the curve.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand yields close lower across the curve.

text.p: New Zealand debt securities closed well bid on Tuesday with yields lower across the curve.
Dealers said the short end was stronger on the back of a rally in Australia and a successful T-bill tender today.
"The market just appeared a little short in the short end," a money market trader said.

"The T-bill tender went off very well this afternoon. There were a lot of T-bills issued today -- $500 million as opposed to the usual $200 (million), and the market took that in its stride and it's just kept a bid tone on it today."
The 90-day bank bill rate edged a couple of pips lower to 9.91 percent.

On Friday, the Reserve Bank will report its September economic projections, and while economists believe it will maintain its currently tight monetary policy settings, they say it may fail to comment if short rates were nudged lower.
The central bank is widely expected to ease conditions by early next year.
"The market seems to think we're going to get something pretty positive on Friday," said a dealer. "We just seem to be drifting down into the statement on Friday."
Another said the strength of the December futures contract, up three points to 90.73, indicated that the market had started to price in "a bit of an easing" already.
Bond yields were between six and eight basis points lower, primarily in response to stronger offshore markets, dealers said.
"The Aussie market's rallied, the U.S. market's rallying -- that will tend to pull our market (yields) down with it," a dealer said, adding that trade had been light throughout the session.
There appeared to be room for yields to move lower across the curve this week, although the market was expected to draw breath as the RBNZ statement neared.
A futures close-out on Wednesday would also constitute "a day in itself" for the short end, one dealer noted.
